TP4, DSpark with a fixed 3.51 accepted tokens per step, 8K input / 1K output tokens, closed loop at each concurrency; one server per column, two rounds (the second in reverse concurrency order), mean shown; % vs `main`. This PR is the **+ #44626** column.

| Concurrency | Metric | `main` | **+ #44626** | + #44628 | + #44627 |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Decode step p50 (ms) | 4.850 | **4.162 (-14.2%)** | 4.062 (-16.2%) | 4.082 (-15.8%) |
|  | tok/s/user p50 | 724 | **836 (+15.5%)** | 864 (+19.3%) | 864 (+19.3%) |
|  | Output tok/s | 641 | **723 (+12.8%)** | 743 (+15.9%) | 765 (+19.3%) |
|  | TTFT p50 (ms) | 187 | **188 (+0.5%)** | 191 (+2.1%) | 145 (-22.5%) |
| 2 | Decode step p50 (ms) | 5.735 | **4.623 (-19.4%)** | 4.533 (-21.0%) | 4.485 (-21.8%) |
|  | tok/s/user p50 | 614 | **754 (+22.8%)** | 774 (+26.1%) | 768 (+25.1%) |
|  | Output tok/s | 1,001 | **1,169 (+16.8%)** | 1,209 (+20.8%) | 1,281 (+28.0%) |
|  | TTFT p50 (ms) | 363 | **366 (+0.8%)** | 365 (+0.6%) | 280 (-22.9%) |
| 4 | Decode step p50 (ms) | 6.649 | **5.558 (-16.4%)** | 5.460 (-17.9%) | 5.514 (-17.1%) |
|  | tok/s/user p50 | 492 | **606 (+23.2%)** | 616 (+25.2%) | 585 (+18.9%) |
|  | Output tok/s | 1,519 | **1,733 (+14.1%)** | 1,757 (+15.7%) | 1,875 (+23.4%) |
|  | TTFT p50 (ms) | 712 | **715 (+0.4%)** | 708 (-0.6%) | 494 (-30.6%) |
| 8 | Decode step p50 (ms) | 8.473 | **7.755 (-8.5%)** | 7.591 (-10.4%) | 7.656 (-9.6%) |
|  | tok/s/user p50 | 355 | **381 (+7.3%)** | 390 (+9.9%) | 390 (+9.9%) |
|  | Output tok/s | 2,085 | **2,186 (+4.8%)** | 2,227 (+6.8%) | 2,444 (+17.2%) |
|  | TTFT p50 (ms) | 1,069 | **1,082 (+1.2%)** | 1,066 (-0.3%) | 769 (-28.1%) |

#44626 shortens the decode step by 8.5-19.4% against `main`. #44628 takes another 0.09-0.16 ms off (1.8-2.4%). #44627 leaves the decode step unchanged within round noise (-0.05 to +0.07 ms) and cuts TTFT by 23-30% with the prefill CUDA graph, which lifts output throughput at concurrency 8 from 2,227 to 2,444 tok/s. All three together: decode step -9.6% to -21.8%, tok/s/user +9.9% to +25.1%, output tok/s +17.2% to +28.0%.

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "tok/s/user p50 (higher is better): bars = main; lines = + #44626, + #44628, + #44627"
    x-axis "Concurrency" ["1", "2", "4", "8"]
    y-axis "tok/s/user" 0 --> 900
    bar [724, 614, 492, 355]
    line [836, 754, 606, 381]
    line [864, 774, 616, 390]
    line [864, 768, 585, 390]
```

Agentic workloads such as the InferenceX AgentX traces send long, mostly prefix-cached conversations and wait for each reply before sending the next turn. A DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash server therefore decodes only a few requests at a time with DSpark speculative decoding (6 verify rows per request), and users see the time per output token.

At these batch sizes a decode step on one GB300 node (TP4) is a long chain of small kernels, several of them sized for larger batches:

- `wqkv_a`, `wq_b` and `wo_b` run the persistent CuTe DSL MXFP8 GEMM.
- The routed experts run FlashInfer's TRT-LLM-gen routing and batched GEMMs, tuned for larger M.
- The compressor and indexer projections give cuBLAS and the JIT small GEMMs only a few output tiles, and the indexer query waits behind `wq_b` on the sources stream.
- `wo_b` writes its rows to memory, and the fused all-reduce + mHC kernel reads them back.
- The LM head runs cuBLAS split-K plus a reduce.
- Past 8 rows, sparse decode attention leaves the 16-head swap-AB kernel for FlashMLA on 64 heads, 48 of them zero padding at TP4.

This PR adds an opt-in switch, `--enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode`, that replaces these calls with kernels sized for 1 to 48 rows on the deployment it was validated on. With the switch on, the decode step is 15.2%, 20.0%, 16.3% and 8.2% shorter at batch 1, 2, 4 and 8 than with it off, measured on one node. With the switch off, the model runs as on `main`.

A stacked follow-up PR puts the DSpark draft model on the same paths.

## Modifications

All new code is in `python/sglang/srt/models/dsv41_low_latency/` (README inside). Each adapted file names its source and keeps that source's SPDX and copyright headers.

| Path | Why | Rows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wqkv_a`, `wq_b`, `wo_b` on FlashInfer's `cutedsl_low_latency` MXFP8 GEMM; the 5-8-row tactic pinned per GB300 shape during startup autotune (`mxfp8_linear.py`) | The persistent kernel is sized for larger batches. The pinned tactics were picked jointly over a 40-layer chain; a single-call autotune picks worse ones. | 1-8 |
| `wo_b`'s epilogue publishes its rows into the mailbox of a Lamport all-reduce + mHC kernel; the attention boundary launches only the consumer (`wo_b_publish.py`, `lamport/`) | Removes the store and reload between `wo_b` and the fused post. | 1-8 |
| Routed experts on one route kernel and two `tcgen05` block-scaled GEMMs of 8-row tiles, NVRTC-compiled and cached; an expert chosen by more than 8 rows gets several tiles (`routed_expert_gemm.py`, `routed_expert_gemm_src/`) | FlashInfer's routing + batched GEMMs are tuned for larger M. The pair returns FlashInfer's deferred-finalize triple, so the fused finalize + all-reduce + mHC consumer is unchanged. | 1-48 |
| Compressor `wkv` / `wkv_gate` and indexer `weights_proj` / `wk` on split-K low-M BF16 GEMMs; the indexer query (`weights_proj`, `wq_b`, RoPE + FP4 pack) on its own side stream (`indexer.py`, `low_m_gemm.py`, `ll_bf16/`) | Skinny shapes; the query reads only `x` and `q_lora`. | 1-8 |
| LM head on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL low-M BF16 GEMM (`lm_head.py`) | cuBLAS split-K plus a reduce kernel. | 1-16 |
| Gluon swap-AB sparse decode attention up to 24 rows, launched with PDL, with a one-warp combine | FlashMLA pads to 64 heads. PDL lets `wo_a_fused` stream its weights during the attention; the narrow combine is 2.1 vs 3.1 µs at 12 rows. | 6-24 |

**The switch and its refusal.** `--enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode` (an `ExecFeatures` field, with a row in `server_arguments.mdx`) is validated on one deployment. `validate_deepseek_v41_features` calls `switch.check_deployment`, which raises once and lists every unmet requirement:

- DeepSeek-V4.1 on one SM103 node, `--tp-size 4`;
- `--ep-size 1` and `--moe-a2a-backend none`;
- no PP, DP attention or CP, and no two-batch overlap;
- `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, the default DSV4 attention backend, and decode CUDA graphs;
- no SWA bounded replay, PD disaggregation, LoRA or deterministic inference;
- no `--enable-fp32-lm-head` and no `--rl-on-policy-target`.

**Hooks outside the package** (+316 / −46 lines in 15 files). Each stock class gains one `None` override field plus one guarded call, and `install.py` sets the fields once the target model is built. With the switch off, every field stays `None`.

- `fp8.py`: `Fp8LinearMethod.mxfp8_cutedsl_override`.
- `mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py`: `low_batch_gemm_factory` / `low_batch_gemm`, used only on deferred-finalize calls.
- `dsv41_sparse.py`: compressor `low_m_bf16_gemm` / `low_m_fp32_gemm` (and `project_kv` for the ratio-1 projection), indexer `low_m_gemm`.
- `deepseek_v4_backend.py`, `v41_indexer/{scoring,types}.py`: the prepared index query of a decode step, and the swap-AB row bound / PDL / narrow combine as backend attributes.
- `decode_attention_sm100{,_gluon}.py`: `max_rows`, `pdl` and `narrow_combine` arguments (defaults keep today's kernels).
- `deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_v4_boundary.py`, `deepseek_v4_mhc.py`: the `wo_b_publish` and `low_latency_index_q` fields, `defers_attn_sum` (now shared by the attention transport and the publisher), the install calls, and the mailbox consumer in `run_attn_post`.
- `flashinfer_autotune.py`: the pinned-tactic context and an autotune cache-key part.
- The LM head is a `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` subclass, so `logits_processor.py` and the DSpark draft's LM-head call are untouched.

**Rank lockstep.** The mailbox and the fused all-reduce are collectives, so every rank must take the same path at every step. Each gate reads only host state that all TP ranks share: row counts and load-time facts. A wo_b publish happens only when the attention transport defers its sum to the fused post (`defers_attn_sum`), and a second publish before the first was reduced raises instead of desynchronizing the mailbox.

## Accuracy Tests

`sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 4096` (sgl-eval 0.1.2, temperature 0), DSpark with real acceptance, GB300 TP4:

| arm | GSM8K-200 |
| --- | --- |
| this PR, switch off (cookbook EP4 launch), image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261012` | 0.980 |
| this PR, switch on (`--ep-size 1 --enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode`), same image | 0.980 |

Error rate 0 and truncation 0 in both runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Repro.** One GB300 node (4 GPUs), image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935`, this branch mounted as the source. Switch-off arm (the cookbook GB300 low-latency launch, with decode graphs to batch 8):

```bash
SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=rng \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 --max-running-requests 16 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
```

Switch-on arm: the same command with `--ep-size 1 --enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode`.

The `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` variables fix the accepted length at 3.51 tokens per step (the AgentX average), so both arms decode the same number of steps. Client: streaming `/generate` requests with 8,192 random input token ids (seeded per point, identical across arms), 1,024 output tokens, `ignore_eos`, temperature 0. The client runs a closed loop at concurrency C: 2·C warm-up requests, then 5·C timed requests. The **step** is the median gap between streamed chunks; each chunk is one speculative step.

**Decode step, same node, one server per launch, both arms from this branch's head.** The launches ran in the order switch off, switch on, `main`. Each launch ran two rounds, the second in reverse concurrency order; the table shows the mean of the two.

| Batch (rows) | Switch off (ms) | Switch on (ms) | Change | `main` (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 (6) | 4.912 | 4.164 | −15.2% | 4.884 |
| 2 (12) | 5.703 | 4.564 | −20.0% | |
| 4 (24) | 6.637 | 5.552 | −16.3% | |
| 8 (48) | 8.417 | 7.729 | −8.2% | 8.402 |

- Every switch-on round is below every switch-off round at every batch. Rounds within an arm differ by at most 0.09 ms.
- With the switch off the branch measures as `main` (+0.03 ms at batch 1, +0.02 ms at batch 8, within round noise).
- Output throughput at batch 8: 2,069 tok/s off, 2,177 on, 2,083 on `main`. TTFT is unchanged (prefill takes the stock path): 192-198 ms off, 184-185 ms on at batch 1.
- `--ep-size 1` alone (switch off) accounts for part of the gain. In an earlier same-node run without the swap-AB PDL commit, it took the switch-off step from 4.871 to 4.601 ms at batch 1 and from 8.453 to 8.023 ms at batch 8; the switch's kernels then made the rest.

**Which paths ran.** A torch-profiler window of 30 decode steps at batch 1 (TP0, switch on) shows every path's kernels:

- `dsv41_routed_expert_route` / `gemm1` / `gemm2`: 1,160 each (40 MoE layers × 29 steps).
- `PublishingLowLatencyBlockscaledGemmKernel` and the Lamport consumer: 1,160 each.
- FlashInfer `LowLatencyBlockscaledGemmKernel`: 2,320.
- `LLBf16Dotprod`: 232.
- Swap-AB `partial_gluon` + `_combine`: 1,247 each.

The remaining FlashInfer MoE and persistent MXFP8 calls belong to the DSpark draft and the shared experts, which the follow-up PR covers. No arm logged a serving-time compile or an error line.

## Tests

```bash
# CPU and one-GPU tests (the GPU cases skip without an SM100-family GPU)
python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_dsv41_low_latency_switch.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp8_low_latency_pinned_tactics.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/test_low_latency_lm_head.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsv41_low_latency_compressor.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsv41_low_latency_indexer.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/moe/test_dsv41_routed_expert_gemm_wide.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v41_wo_b_publish.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/test_swapab_attention.py
# Four GPUs: the publishing wo_b GEMM and the Lamport consumer against FlashInfer + a separate publish
torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_dsv41_wo_b_publish.py
```

| Check | What it covers | Result (GB300) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Switch | Every refusal reported on its own and all together in one error; the validated deployment passes; the row bounds | Passed |
| Kernel tests | Low-latency MXFP8 vs the stock GEMM and the pinned-tactic plumbing; the LM head; the compressor and indexer projections and the side-stream index query (bit-equal to the serial one, eager and graph replay); routed experts at 1-48 rows vs FlashInfer (eager and graph); swap-AB attention to 24 rows with PDL and the narrow combine (eager and graph); the wo_b publisher's gating | 77 passed, 179 subtests (plus the pipeline / boundary tests whose fakes gained the new fields) |
| Four-rank wo_b publish | Published rows and the consumer bit-equal to FlashInfer's GEMM + a separate publish; an installed layer publishes only when the boundary defers its sum | 2 passed on each rank |
| pre-commit | All hooks on every changed file | Passes |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

- `dsv41_sparse.py`: compressor `low_m_bf16_gemm` / `low_m_fp32_gemm` (and `project_kv` for the ratio-1 projection), indexer `low_m_gemm`.
- `deepseek_v4_backend.py`, `v41_indexer/{scoring,types}.py`: the prepared index query of a decode step, and the swap-AB row bound / PDL / narrow combine as backend attributes.
- `decode_attention_sm100{,_gluon}.py`: `max_rows`, `pdl` and `narrow_combine` arguments (defaults keep today's kernels).
- `deepseek_v4.py`, `deepseek_v4_boundary.py`, `deepseek_v4_mhc.py`: the `wo_b_publish` and `low_latency_index_q` fields, `defers_attn_sum` (now shared by the attention transport and the publisher), the install calls, and the mailbox consumer in `run_attn_post`.
- `flashinfer_autotune.py`: the pinned-tactic context and an autotune cache-key part.
- The LM head is a `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` subclass, so `logits_processor.py` and the DSpark draft's LM-head call are untouched.

**Rank lockstep.** The mailbox and the fused all-reduce are collectives, so every rank must take the same path at every step. Each gate reads only host state that all TP ranks share: row counts and load-time facts. A wo_b publish happens only when the attention transport defers its sum to the fused post (`defers_attn_sum`), and a second publish before the first was reduced raises instead of desynchronizing the mailbox.

## Accuracy Tests

`sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 4096` (sgl-eval 0.1.2, temperature 0), DSpark with real acceptance, GB300 TP4:

| arm | GSM8K-200 |
| --- | --- |
| this PR, switch off (cookbook EP4 launch), image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261012` | 0.980 |
| this PR, switch on (`--ep-size 1 --enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode`), same image | 0.980 |

Error rate 0 and truncation 0 in both runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Repro.** One GB300 node (4 GPUs), image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935`, this branch mounted as the source. Switch-off arm (the cookbook GB300 low-latency launch, with decode graphs to batch 8):

```bash
SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=rng \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 --max-running-requests 16 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
```

Switch-on arm: the same command with `--ep-size 1 --enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode`.

The `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` variables fix the accepted length at 3.51 tokens per step (the AgentX average), so both arms decode the same number of steps. Client: streaming `/generate` requests with 8,192 random input token ids (seeded per point, identical across arms), 1,024 output tokens, `ignore_eos`, temperature 0. The client runs a closed loop at concurrency C: 2·C warm-up requests, then 5·C timed requests. The **step** is the median gap between streamed chunks; each chunk is one speculative step.

**Decode step, same node, one server per launch, both arms from this branch's head.** The launches ran in the order switch off, switch on, `main`. Each launch ran two rounds, the second in reverse concurrency order; the table shows the mean of the two.

| Batch (rows) | Switch off (ms) | Switch on (ms) | Change | `main` (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 (6) | 4.912 | 4.164 | −15.2% | 4.884 |
| 2 (12) | 5.703 | 4.564 | −20.0% | |
| 4 (24) | 6.637 | 5.552 | −16.3% | |
| 8 (48) | 8.417 | 7.729 | −8.2% | 8.402 |

- Every switch-on round is below every switch-off round at every batch. Rounds within an arm differ by at most 0.09 ms.
- With the switch off the branch measures as `main` (+0.03 ms at batch 1, +0.02 ms at batch 8, within round noise).
- Output throughput at batch 8: 2,069 tok/s off, 2,177 on, 2,083 on `main`. TTFT is unchanged (prefill takes the stock path): 192-198 ms off, 184-185 ms on at batch 1.
- `--ep-size 1` alone (switch off) accounts for part of the gain. In an earlier same-node run without the swap-AB PDL commit, it took the switch-off step from 4.871 to 4.601 ms at batch 1 and from 8.453 to 8.023 ms at batch 8; the switch's kernels then made the rest.

**Which paths ran.** A torch-profiler window of 30 decode steps at batch 1 (TP0, switch on) shows every path's kernels:

- `dsv41_routed_expert_route` / `gemm1` / `gemm2`: 1,160 each (40 MoE layers × 29 steps).
- `PublishingLowLatencyBlockscaledGemmKernel` and the Lamport consumer: 1,160 each.
- FlashInfer `LowLatencyBlockscaledGemmKernel`: 2,320.
- `LLBf16Dotprod`: 232.
- Swap-AB `partial_gluon` + `_combine`: 1,247 each.

The remaining FlashInfer MoE and persistent MXFP8 calls belong to the DSpark draft and the shared experts, which the follow-up PR covers. No arm logged a serving-time compile or an error line.

```bash

python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/models/test_dsv41_low_latency_switch.py \

torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_dsv41_wo_b_publish.py
```

+# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash low-latency decode (GB300)
+
+`--enable-dsv41-low-latency-decode` replaces a set of stock decode kernels of
+DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with kernels sized for 1 to 48 rows. It targets agentic
+serving, where a server decodes a handful of requests at a time with DSpark
+speculative decoding and users see the time per output token.
+
+With the switch off, nothing in this package runs and the model takes the stock
+paths.
+
+## Validated deployment
+
+The switch refuses every other deployment at startup, listing each requirement
+it misses (`switch.check_deployment`):
+
+- DeepSeek-V4.1, one SM103 node (GB300 / B300), `--tp-size 4`;
+- `--ep-size 1` and `--moe-a2a-backend none` (the routed-expert GEMMs serve
+  every expert locally);
+- no pipeline, DP-attention or context parallelism, no two-batch overlap;
+- `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, the default DeepSeek-V4 attention backend,
+  decode CUDA graphs;
+- no encoder or decoder SWA bounded replay, PD disaggregation, LoRA or
+  deterministic inference;
+- no `--enable-fp32-lm-head` or `--rl-on-policy-target` (the low-M LM head
+  returns BF16 logits).
+
+## Paths
+
+Each path replaces one stock call. It runs only inside its row bound
+(`switch.py`) and otherwise declines, so the stock kernel runs. Rows are the
+tokens of one forward: a DSpark verify step at batch `b` has `6 b` rows.
+
+| Path | Replaces | Rows | Module |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `wqkv_a`, `wq_b`, `wo_b` on FlashInfer's `cutedsl_low_latency` MXFP8 GEMM, tactics pinned per GB300 shape | the persistent CuTe DSL MXFP8 GEMM | 1-8 | `mxfp8_linear.py` |
+| `wo_b`'s epilogue stores its rows into the Lamport mailbox; the attention boundary runs only the all-reduce + mHC consumer | `wo_b` + the fused all-reduce + mHC post | 1-8 | `wo_b_publish.py`, `lamport/` |
+| Routed experts: one route kernel + two `tcgen05` GEMMs (8-row tiles; an expert chosen by more rows gets several tiles), NVRTC-compiled | FlashInfer TRT-LLM-gen routing + batched GEMMs | 1-48 | `routed_expert_gemm.py`, `routed_expert_gemm_src/` |
+| Compressor `wkv` / `wkv_gate`, indexer `weights_proj` and `wk` on split-K low-M BF16 GEMMs | cuBLAS and the JIT small GEMMs | 1-8 | `indexer.py`, `low_m_gemm.py`, `ll_bf16/` |
+| Indexer query (`weights_proj`, `wq_b`, RoPE + FP4 pack) on a side stream beside `wqkv_a` and the compressor | the same work on the sources stream | low-ratio decode | `indexer.py` |
+| LM head (shared with the DSpark draft) on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL low-M BF16 GEMM | cuBLAS split-K + reduce | 1-16 | `lm_head.py` |
+| Gluon swap-AB sparse decode attention up to 24 rows, launched with PDL, one-warp combine | FlashMLA sparse decode on 64 zero-padded heads past 8 rows | 6-24 | `switch.SWAPAB_MAX_ROWS` |
+
+## Rank lockstep
+
+The fused all-reduce and the mailbox are collectives, so every rank must take the
+same path at every step. Each gate reads only host state that all TP ranks share:
+row counts, the graph mode and load-time facts. Nothing is read back from the GPU.
+A publish whose rows were not reduced by the fused post raises instead of
+desynchronizing the mailbox.
+
+## Startup
+
+The MXFP8 projections are tuned at 1, 2, 4 and 8 rows during FlashInfer's
+startup autotune, with the pinned tactic as the only choice for 5-8 rows; the
+autotune cache key records the switch. The routed-expert GEMMs are compiled with
+NVRTC on first use and cached under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/dsv41_routed_expert_gemm`.
+The mailbox and its publishing GEMM are built on the first eager forward, never
+during graph capture.
+
+## Provenance
+
+The routed-expert GEMMs, the wo_b publish, the Lamport all-reduce + mHC changes and the low-M projections were developed at NVIDIA for this model. Files derived from vLLM (vllm-project/vllm@75e3b17c) or FlashInfer keep those projects' SPDX and copyright headers.

+def _ll_bf16_gemm(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    from sglang.srt.models.dsv41_low_latency.ll_bf16 import ll_bf16_gemm
+

+def _bf16_rounded(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    # FP32 accumulation rounded to the layer's BF16 output.
+    if not fits(x, LOW_M_BF16_MAX_ROWS):
+        return None
+    return _ll_bf16_gemm(x, weight).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _fp32(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    return _ll_bf16_gemm(x, weight) if fits(x, LOW_M_BF16_MAX_ROWS) else None
+
+
+def _bf16(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    return cutedsl_low_m_mm(x, weight) if fits(x, LOW_M_BF16_MAX_ROWS) else None
+

+def install_projections(attn: nn.Module) -> None:
+    """The compressor's ratio-1 wkv (BF16 out) and ratio-2 wkv_gate (FP32 out), the
+    indexer's weights_proj and wk: split-K GEMMs at 1-8 rows instead of cuBLAS or
+    the JIT small GEMMs, which give few output tiles to these skinny shapes."""
+    if not (ll_bf16_supported() and cutedsl_low_m_supported()):
+        return
+    if attn.compressor is not None:
+        attn.compressor.low_m_bf16_gemm = _bf16
+        attn.compressor.low_m_fp32_gemm = _fp32
+    if attn.indexer is not None:
+        attn.indexer.low_m_gemm = _bf16_rounded

+class IndexQ:
+    """One decode step's index query, built on a side stream beside wqkv_a, wq_b
+    and the compressor; the scoring on the sources stream waits for it."""
+
+    def __init__(self, stream: torch.cuda.Stream, head_weights_raw: torch.Tensor):
+        self.stream = stream
+        self._head_weights_raw = head_weights_raw
+
+    def finish(
+        self,
+        *,
+        layer: nn.Module,
+        q_lora: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        forward_batch,
+        attn_backend,
+        stream_sources: torch.cuda.Stream,
+    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        self.stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(self.stream):
+            q, _ = layer.indexer.wq_b(q_lora)
+            prepared = attn_backend.low_ratio_decode_index_q(
+                layer=layer,
+                q=q,
+                head_weights_raw=self._head_weights_raw,
+                positions=positions,
+                forward_batch=forward_batch,
+            )
+        stream_sources.wait_stream(self.stream)
+        return prepared
+
+
+class IndexQSideStream:
+    def __init__(self, stream: torch.cuda.Stream):
+        self._stream = stream
+
+    def begin(
+        self, layer: nn.Module, x: torch.Tensor, attn_backend
+    ) -> Optional[IndexQ]:
+        """Start weights_proj, which reads only x; None keeps the stock order."""
+        if layer.indexer is None or not attn_backend.low_ratio_decode_reads_prepared_q:
+            return None
+        self._stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(self._stream):
+            head_weights_raw = layer.indexer.head_weights_raw(x)
+        return IndexQ(self._stream, head_weights_raw)
+
+
+def install_index_q_side_stream(attn: nn.Module) -> None:
+    if attn.indexer is not None and attn.alt_streams is not None:
+        # The low-ratio prepare leaves this one of the layer's three streams idle.
+        attn.low_latency_index_q = IndexQSideStream(attn.alt_streams[1])

+"""Lamport all-reduce fused with DSV4.1's mHC post, collapse and RMSNorm.
+
+FlashInfer's LL kernels, copied: a publish kernel (or its MoE finalize
+variant) multicasts each rank's contribution into a three-generation Lamport
+mailbox, and a PDL-chained consumer spins until every rank's fragment lands,
+reduces it and normalizes. The consumer's residual add and copy are replaced by
+the mHC post-mix of the hc residual streams and their pre-mix collapse, which
+the RMSNorm then normalizes. The finalize variant also reads FP32 routing
+weights.
+
+Optionally the consumer also writes the normalized output as MXFP8 with UE8M0
+scales in the swizzled 128x4 layout FlashInfer's MXFP8 GEMMs read. It quantizes
+the BF16-rounded output with FlashInfer's own quantize helpers, so the result is
+bit-identical to ``mxfp8_quantize`` of the BF16 output, without its launch.

+NEXT_STAGE = 0
+ACTIVE_STAGE = 1

+MXFP8_BLOCK = 32
+FRAGMENTS_PER_MXFP8_BLOCK = MXFP8_BLOCK // VEC_BF16

+@cute.jit
+def _group_leader_block_sum(
+    value: Float32,
+    warp_sums: cute.Tensor,
+    warps: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+    leader_stride: cutlass.Constexpr[int],
+) -> Float32:
+    lane = cute.arch.lane_idx()
+    warp = cute.arch.warp_idx()
+    for offset in cutlass.range_constexpr(1, WARP_SIZE):
+        if cutlass.const_expr(offset >= leader_stride and (offset & (offset - 1)) == 0):
+            value = value + cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(
+                value,
+                offset=offset,
+                mask=-1,
+                mask_and_clamp=31,
+            )
+    if lane == 0:
+        cute.arch.store((warp_sums + warp).llvm_ptr, value)
+    cute.arch.barrier()
+
+    result = Float32(0.0)
+    if warp == 0:
+        if lane < Int32(warps):
+            result = cute.arch.load(
+                (warp_sums + lane).llvm_ptr,
+                Float32,
+            )
+        result = cute.arch.warp_reduction_sum(result)
+        if lane == 0:
+            cute.arch.store(warp_sums.llvm_ptr, result)
+    cute.arch.barrier()
+    return cute.arch.load(warp_sums.llvm_ptr, Float32)

+class _SharedOnlyPublishDeviceKernel:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        hidden: int,
+        tp: int,
+        rank: int,
+        capacity_m: int,
+        elements_per_thread: int,
+        threads: int,
+        release_before_store: bool,
+        enable_pdl: bool,
+    ) -> None:
+        if elements_per_thread not in (1, QUAD_BF16, VEC_BF16):
+            raise ValueError("elements_per_thread must be 1, 4, or 8")
+        if hidden <= 0 or hidden % elements_per_thread:
+            raise ValueError("hidden must divide evenly across thread fragments")
+        self.hidden = hidden
+        self.tp = tp
+        self.rank = rank
+        self.capacity_m = capacity_m
+        self.elements_per_thread = elements_per_thread
+        self.threads = threads
+        self.fragments = hidden // elements_per_thread
+        self.ctas_per_token = math.ceil(self.fragments / threads)
+        self.release_before_store = release_before_store
+        self.enable_pdl = enable_pdl
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        shared_output: cute.Tensor,
+        stage_state: cute.Tensor,
+        contribution_mailbox_multicast_address: Int64,
+        m: Int32,
+        stream: cuda.CUstream,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.kernel(
+            shared_output,
+            stage_state,
+            contribution_mailbox_multicast_address,
+        ).launch(
+            grid=(m * self.ctas_per_token, 1, 1),
+            block=(self.threads, 1, 1),
+            stream=stream,
+            use_pdl=self.enable_pdl,
+        )
+
+    @cute.kernel
+    def kernel(
+        self,
+        shared_output: cute.Tensor,
+        stage_state: cute.Tensor,
+        contribution_mailbox_multicast_address: Int64,
+    ) -> None:
+        block, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+        tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+        token = block // self.ctas_per_token
+        cta_in_token = block % self.ctas_per_token
+        fragment = cta_in_token * self.threads + tidx
+
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.enable_pdl):
+            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.elements_per_thread == 1):
+            bits = Uint32(0)
+            if fragment < self.fragments:
+                element = Int64(token) * self.hidden + Int64(fragment)
+                bits = f32_to_bf16_bits(
+                    load_global_bf16_as_f32(
+                        Int64((shared_output.iterator + element).toint())
+                    )
+                )
+                if bits == Uint32(NEGATIVE_ZERO_BF16_BITS):
+                    bits = Uint32(0)
+            partner_bits = shuffle_sync_idx_u32(
+                bits,
+                Int32(cute.arch.lane_idx() | Int32(1)),
+            )
+            packed_word = bits | (partner_bits << Uint32(16))
+        elif cutlass.const_expr(self.elements_per_thread == QUAD_BF16):
+            packed_words = cute.make_rmem_tensor(cute.make_layout((2,)), Uint32)
+            packed_words.fill(Uint32(0))
+            if fragment < self.fragments:
+                element = Int64(token) * self.hidden + Int64(fragment) * QUAD_BF16
+                pointer = cute.make_ptr(
+                    BFloat16,
+                    (shared_output.iterator + element).llvm_ptr,
+                    cute.AddressSpace.gmem,
+                    assumed_align=8,
+                )
+                packed_words.store(
+                    sanitize_negative_zero_u32x2(load_global_u32x2(pointer))
+                )
+        else:
+            packed_words = cute.make_rmem_tensor(cute.make_layout((4,)), Uint32)
+            packed_words.fill(Uint32(0))
+            if fragment < self.fragments:
+                element = Int64(token) * self.hidden + Int64(fragment) * VEC_BF16
+                pointer = cute.make_ptr(
+                    BFloat16,
+                    (shared_output.iterator + element).llvm_ptr,
+                    cute.AddressSpace.gmem,
+                    assumed_align=16,
+                )
+                packed_words.store(
+                    sanitize_negative_zero_u32x4(load_global_u32x4(pointer))
+                )
+
+        stage = load_volatile_u32(stage_state.iterator + NEXT_STAGE)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.release_before_store):
+            if block == 0 and tidx == 0:
+                store_global_u32(
+                    stage_state.iterator + ACTIVE_STAGE,
+                    stage,
+                )
+            cute.arch.barrier()
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.enable_pdl):
+                cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.elements_per_thread == 1):
+            if (cute.arch.lane_idx() & Int32(1)) == Int32(
+                0
+            ) and fragment < self.fragments:
+                mailbox_element = (
+                    (Int64(stage) * self.tp + self.rank) * self.capacity_m
+                    + Int64(token)
+                ) * self.hidden + Int64(fragment)
+                stmc_bf16x2(
+                    contribution_mailbox_multicast_address + mailbox_element * 2,
+                    packed_word,
+                )
+        elif cutlass.const_expr(self.elements_per_thread == QUAD_BF16):
+            if fragment < self.fragments:
+                mailbox_element = (
+                    (Int64(stage) * self.tp + self.rank) * self.capacity_m
+                    + Int64(token)
+                ) * self.hidden + Int64(fragment) * QUAD_BF16
+                stmc_bf16x4(
+                    contribution_mailbox_multicast_address + mailbox_element * 2,
+                    packed_words,
+                )
+        else:
+            if fragment < self.fragments:
+                mailbox_element = (
+                    (Int64(stage) * self.tp + self.rank) * self.capacity_m
+                    + Int64(token)
+                ) * self.hidden + Int64(fragment) * VEC_BF16
+                stmc_bf16x8(
+                    contribution_mailbox_multicast_address + mailbox_element * 2,
+                    packed_words,
+                )
+
+        if cutlass.const_expr(not self.release_before_store):
+            if block == 0 and tidx == 0:
+                store_global_u32(
+                    stage_state.iterator + ACTIVE_STAGE,
+                    stage,
+                )
+            cute.arch.barrier()
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.enable_pdl):
+                cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+

+class _QuadFinalizePublishDeviceKernel:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        hidden: int,
+        top_k: int,
+        tp: int,
+        rank: int,
+        capacity_m: int,
+        threads: int,
+        routed_scaling_factor: float,
+        include_shared_expert: bool,
+        load_shared_expert_before_pdl: bool,
+        enable_pdl: bool,
+        prefetch_group: int,
+        fp32_weights: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        if hidden <= 0 or hidden % QUAD_BF16:
+            raise ValueError("hidden must be a positive multiple of 4")
+        self.hidden = hidden
+        self.top_k = top_k
+        self.tp = tp
+        self.rank = rank
+        self.capacity_m = capacity_m
+        self.threads = threads
+        self.routed_scaling_factor = routed_scaling_factor
+        self.fragments = hidden // QUAD_BF16
+        self.ctas_per_token = math.ceil(self.fragments / threads)
+        self.include_shared_expert = include_shared_expert
+        self.load_shared_expert_before_pdl = load_shared_expert_before_pdl
+        self.enable_pdl = enable_pdl
+        self.prefetch_group = prefetch_group
+        self.prefetch_groups = (top_k + prefetch_group - 1) // prefetch_group
+        self.fp32_weights = fp32_weights
+
+    def smem_size_in_bytes(self) -> int:
+        return self.top_k * 8
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        routed_output: cute.Tensor,
+        expert_weights: cute.Tensor,
+        permuted_indices: cute.Tensor,
+        shared_output: cute.Tensor,
+        stage_state: cute.Tensor,
+        contribution_mailbox_multicast_address: Int64,
+        m: Int32,
+        stream: cuda.CUstream,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.kernel(
+            routed_output,
+            expert_weights,
+            permuted_indices,
+            shared_output,
+            stage_state,
+            contribution_mailbox_multicast_address,
+        ).launch(
+            grid=(m * self.ctas_per_token, 1, 1),
+            block=(self.threads, 1, 1),
+            smem=self.smem_size_in_bytes(),
+            stream=stream,
+            use_pdl=self.enable_pdl,
+        )
+
+    @cute.kernel
+    def kernel(
+        self,
+        routed_output: cute.Tensor,
+        expert_weights: cute.Tensor,
+        permuted_indices: cute.Tensor,
+        shared_output: cute.Tensor,
+        stage_state: cute.Tensor,
+        contribution_mailbox_multicast_address: Int64,
+    ) -> None:
+        block, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+        tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+        token = block // self.ctas_per_token
+        cta_in_token = block % self.ctas_per_token
+        fragment = cta_in_token * self.threads + tidx
+
+        smem = cutlass.utils.SmemAllocator()
+        staged_indices = smem.allocate_array(Int32, self.top_k)
+        staged_weights = smem.allocate_array(Float32, self.top_k)
+        metadata_index = Int32(tidx)
+        while metadata_index < Int32(self.top_k):
+            element = Int64(token) * self.top_k + Int64(metadata_index)
+            row = cute.arch.load(
+                (permuted_indices.iterator + element).llvm_ptr,
+                Int32,
+            )
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.fp32_weights):
+                weight = cute.arch.load(
+                    (expert_weights.iterator + element).llvm_ptr,
+                    Float32,
+                )
+            else:
+                weight = load_global_bf16_as_f32(
+                    Int64((expert_weights.iterator + element).toint())
+                )
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.routed_scaling_factor != 1.0):
+                weight = weight * Float32(self.routed_scaling_factor)
+            if row == Int32(-1):
+                weight = Float32(0.0)
+            cute.arch.store(
+                (staged_indices + metadata_index).llvm_ptr,
+                row,
+            )
+            cute.arch.store(
+                (staged_weights + metadata_index).llvm_ptr,
+                weight,
+            )
+            metadata_index = metadata_index + self.threads
+        cute.arch.barrier()
+
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.include_shared_expert):
+            shared_values = cute.make_rmem_tensor(
+                cute.make_layout((QUAD_BF16,)), BFloat16
+            )
+            shared_values.fill(BFloat16(0.0))
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.load_shared_expert_before_pdl):  # noqa: SIM102
+                if fragment < self.fragments:
+                    shared_element = (
+                        Int64(token) * self.hidden + Int64(fragment) * QUAD_BF16
+                    )
+                    shared_pointer = cute.make_ptr(
+                        BFloat16,
+                        (shared_output.iterator + shared_element).llvm_ptr,
+                        cute.AddressSpace.gmem,
+                        assumed_align=8,
+                    )
+                    shared_values.store(
+                        packed_u32x2_to_bf16x4(load_global_u32x2(shared_pointer))
+                    )

+class _LamportMHCDeviceKernel:
+    """FlashInfer's ``_LamportResidualRMSNormDeviceKernel`` with mHC.

+    streams, stored as the residual output, and their pre-mix collapse, which
+    the unchanged RMSNorm normalizes. With ``quantize``, the normalized output
+    is also written as MXFP8 with swizzled 128x4 UE8M0 scales, including the
+    zero scales of the padding rows up to a multiple of 128. With
+    ``residual_only``, only the residual output is written: the pre-mix, the
+    norm weight and the normalized output are not touched.

+        self,
+        *,
+        hidden: int,
+        hc: int,
+        tp: int,
+        capacity_m: int,
+        cluster_size: int,
+        rank_lanes: int,
+        threads: int,
+        enable_pdl: bool,
+        quantize: bool = False,
+        residual_only: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        if rank_lanes not in (1, 2, 4, 8):
+            raise ValueError("rank_lanes must be 1, 2, 4, or 8")
+        if tp % rank_lanes:
+            raise ValueError("tp must be divisible by rank_lanes")
+        if threads <= 0 or threads % WARP_SIZE or threads % rank_lanes:
+            raise ValueError("threads must be a positive warp and rank-lane multiple")
+        if hidden <= 0 or hidden % VEC_BF16:
+            raise ValueError("hidden must be a positive multiple of 8")
+        # A scale block's four fragments must sit in four adjacent lanes.
+        if quantize and (rank_lanes != 1 or hidden % (MXFP8_BLOCK * SCALE_TILE_COLS)):
+            raise ValueError("MXFP8 output needs rank_lanes == 1 and hidden % 128 == 0")
+        if quantize and residual_only:
+            raise ValueError("a residual-only consumer has no layer input to quantize")
+        self.quantize = quantize
+        self.write_layer_input = not residual_only
+        self.scale_cols = hidden // MXFP8_BLOCK
+        self.hidden = hidden
+        self.hc = hc
+        self.tp = tp
+        self.capacity_m = capacity_m
+        self.cluster_size = cluster_size
+        self.rank_lanes = rank_lanes
+        self.threads = threads
+        self.enable_pdl = enable_pdl
+        self.fragments = hidden // VEC_BF16
+        self.groups_per_cta = threads // rank_lanes
+        self.fragment_stride = cluster_size * self.groups_per_cta
+        self.trips = math.ceil(self.fragments / self.fragment_stride)
+        self.warps = threads // WARP_SIZE

+        return (self.warps + self.cluster_size) * 4

+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        contribution_mailbox: cute.Tensor,
+        residual_source: cute.Tensor,
+        post: cute.Tensor,
+        comb: cute.Tensor,
+        pre: cute.Tensor,
+        gamma: cute.Tensor,
+        residual_output: cute.Tensor,
+        norm_output: cute.Tensor,
+        quant_output: cute.Tensor,
+        quant_scales: cute.Tensor,
+        stage_state: cute.Tensor,
+        eps: Float32,
+        m: Int32,
+        stream: cuda.CUstream,

+            residual_source,
+            post,
+            comb,
+            pre,
+            gamma,
+            residual_output,
+            norm_output,
+            quant_output,
+            quant_scales,
+            stage_state,
+            eps,

+            grid=(m, self.cluster_size, 1),
+            block=(self.threads, 1, 1),
+            cluster=(1, self.cluster_size, 1),

+    @cute.kernel

+        residual_source: cute.Tensor,
+        post: cute.Tensor,
+        comb: cute.Tensor,
+        pre: cute.Tensor,
+        gamma: cute.Tensor,

+class AllReduceMHC:
+    """Lamport TP all-reduce fused with mHC post, collapse and RMSNorm.
+
+    ``__call__`` reduces ``x`` across the TP group, writes the post-mixed hc
+    streams and the normalized collapse, and leaves the next mixes to the
+    caller. ``finalize`` does the same for an unfinalized MoE output, folding
+    the top-k reduction and the shared-expert add into the publish. Each
+    instance owns a Lamport mailbox; construction is collective over the TP
+    group. With ``quantize_layer_input``, both also accept ``mxfp8_out`` buffers
+    that receive the normalized collapse as MXFP8. With ``residual_only``, both
+    also accept ``pre`` and ``norm_weight`` of None and then write only the
+    post-mixed streams, for a consumer that collapses them itself.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        hidden_size: int,
+        hc_mult: int,
+        max_num_tokens: int,
+        top_k: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+        quantize_layer_input: bool = False,
+        residual_only: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        group = get_tp_group().device_group
+        self.hidden_size = hidden = hidden_size
+        self.hc_mult = hc = hc_mult
+        self.capacity = capacity = max_num_tokens
+        self.top_k = top_k
+        self.quantize_layer_input = quantize_layer_input
+        self.residual_only = residual_only
+        self.tp = tp = dist.get_world_size(group)
+        self.rank = rank = dist.get_rank(group)
+        # The contribution a producer already stored into the mailbox (see
+        # ``mark_published``); the next ``__call__`` then only collects.
+        self._published: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        device = torch.device(device)

+    address = pointer.toint(loc=loc, ip=ip)
+    opcode = "ld.volatile.global.v4.u32" if volatile else "ld.global.v4.u32"
+    loaded = _asm(
+        llvm.StructType.get_literal([T.i32()] * 4),
+        [address.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)],
+        f"{opcode} {{$0, $1, $2, $3}}, [$4];",
+        "=r,=r,=r,=r,l",
+        side_effects=volatile,
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+    packed = vector.from_elements(
+        ir.VectorType.get([4], T.i32(), loc=loc),
+        [
+            llvm.extractvalue(T.i32(), loaded, [index], loc=loc, ip=ip)
+            for index in range(4)
+        ],
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )

+projection ``wo_b`` (FlashInfer's ``cutedsl_low_latency`` MXFP8 GEMM for 1 to
+8 rows) writes this rank's partial sum, then a separate publish kernel of
+``AllReduceMHC`` (``_SharedOnlyPublishDeviceKernel``) reads it back and
+multicasts it into the three-generation Lamport mailbox, and only then can the
+``LamportMHC`` consumer start collecting the peers' contributions. The publish
+launch, its grid wait and its read-back sit on the critical path.
+
+Responsibility. :class:`PublishingMxfp8Linear` runs the same GEMM, with the same
+tactic FlashInfer's autotuner selected for the plain call, but its epilogue also
+does the publish kernel's work: every output value goes, rounded to BF16 with
+negative zero cleared, into this rank's slot of the mailbox generation
+``stage_state[0]`` on all ranks (``multimem.st``), and one thread sets
+``stage_state[1]`` to that generation. The caller then calls the same
+``AllReduceMHC`` instance with the returned tensor, which launches only the
+consumer (``AllReduceMHC.mark_published``). The consumer is unchanged, so its
+outputs are bit-identical to the unfused path's.

+GEMM structure. The kernel computes ``C[n, m] = sum_k W[n, k] x[m, k]`` with the
+weight as operand A (128 output columns per CTA, ``N / 128`` CTAs) and the at
+most 8 activation rows as operand B. With split-K ``S`` (the tactic's last

+after the GEMM's programmatic grid wait (the B loads follow it), exactly as the
+publish kernel reads it after its own grid wait; the previous consumer wrote it.

+                    )
+                    mailbox_base = sender_idx * 128 * shard_ept
+                    for i in range(shard_ept):
+                        cute.arch.store_async_dsmem(
+                            dsmem_mailbox_ptr + mailbox_base + i * 128 + epi_tid,
+                            tDrAcc[shard_start + i].bitcast(cutlass.Int32),
+                            mailbox_mbar,
+                            cutlass.Int32(peer),
+                        )
+
+            cute.arch.mbarrier_wait(mailbox_mbar, 0)
+
+            my_shard_start = split_rank * shard_ept
+            for s in range(self.split_k - 1):
+                mailbox_base = s * 128 * shard_ept
+                for i in range(shard_ept):
+                    tDrAcc[my_shard_start + i] = (
+                        tDrAcc[my_shard_start + i]
+                        + (dsmem_mailbox_ptr + mailbox_base + i * 128 + epi_tid).load()
+                    )
+
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.use_scale):
+                tDrAcc.store(tDrAcc.load() * scale_value)
+            if cutlass.const_expr(self.use_bias):
+                tDrAcc.store(tDrAcc.load() + tDrBiasAcc.load())
+
+            for i in range(elems_per_thread):
+                if i < my_shard_start or i >= my_shard_start + shard_ept:
+                    tDpredC[i] = cutlass.Boolean(False)
+
+            acc_vec = tDrAcc.load().to(self.c_dtype)
+            tDrC.store(acc_vec)
+            # PUBLISH: this CTA's shard of rows (the condition is CTA-uniform,
+            # so whole warps shuffle together).
+            for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(elems_per_thread):
+                if i >= my_shard_start and i < my_shard_start + shard_ept:
+                    coord = tDcC[i]
+                    self.publish_value(
+                        f32_to_bf16_bits(tDrC[i].to(Float32)),
+                        coord[0],
+                        coord[1],
+                        tDpredC[i],
+                        stage,
+                        column_lanes,
+                    )
+            cute.basic_copy_if(tDpredC, tDrC, tDgC)
+
+        # PUBLISH: hand the generation to the consumer, once per grid.
+        bidx, bidy, bidz = cute.arch.block_idx()
+        if bidx == 0 and bidy == 0 and bidz == 0 and epi_tid == 0:
+            _store_u32_at(Int64(self.stage_state + ACTIVE_STAGE * 4), stage)
+
+
+def _gmem_ptr(dtype, address: int, align: int):
+    return make_ptr(dtype, address, cute.AddressSpace.gmem, assumed_align=align)
+
+
+class PublishingMxfp8Linear:
+    """Run a low-latency MXFP8 linear whose output an ``AllReduceMHC`` reduces
+    next, publishing the output from the GEMM epilogue.
+
+    ``prepare`` returns None for anything but the inputs the linear's own
+    ``cutedsl_low_latency`` dispatch would take; the caller then runs the linear.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, all_reduce: AllReduceMHC) -> None:
+        self.all_reduce = all_reduce
+        self._compiled: dict[tuple[Tactic, int], object] = {}
+
+    def supports(self, linear: torch.nn.Module, num_tokens: int) -> bool:
+        """Whether ``linear`` on ``num_tokens`` rows runs the publishing GEMM."""
+        return (
+            _is_low_latency_linear(linear)
+            and 0 < num_tokens <= _LOW_LATENCY_MAX_ROWS
+            and num_tokens <= self.all_reduce.capacity
+            and linear.weight.shape[0] == self.all_reduce.hidden_size
+        )
+
+    def prepare(self, linear: torch.nn.Module, x) -> Optional[tuple]:
+        """The low-latency backend's operands for ``linear(x)``, as
+        ``mxfp8_linear`` forms them, or None when it would not
+        take that backend. ``x`` is BF16 or an ``(e4m3, swizzled scales)`` pair."""
+        if not _is_low_latency_linear(linear):
+            return None
+        n, k = linear.weight.shape
+        if isinstance(x, tuple):
+            a, a_scale = x[0].view(-1, k), x[1].reshape(-1)
+            input_shape = x[0].shape
+        else:
+            if x.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+                return None
+            a, a_scale, input_shape = x, None, x.shape
+        if not (
+            self.supports(linear, a.shape[0])
+            and k % 128 == 0
+            and a.is_contiguous()
+            and getattr(linear, "bias", None) is None
+        ):
+            return None
+        if a_scale is None:
+            from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import (
+                flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize,
+            )
+
+            a, a_scale = flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize(
+                a.view(-1, k), is_sf_swizzled_layout=True, alignment=32
+            )
+            a_scale = a_scale.reshape(-1)
+        return a, a_scale, input_shape
+
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        linear: torch.nn.Module,
+        prepared: tuple,
+        *,
+        tactic: Tactic | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """``linear(x)`` for operands from ``prepare``, published into
+        ``all_reduce``'s mailbox; the next ``all_reduce`` call reduces it."""
+        a, a_scale, input_shape = prepared
+        weight = linear.weight
+        weight_scale = linear.weight_scale_inv_swizzled.reshape(-1)
+        n, k = weight.shape
+        m = a.shape[0]
+        out = torch.empty((m, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=a.device)
+        if tactic is None:
+            tactic = _selected_tactic(a, weight.t(), a_scale, weight_scale, out)
+        compiled = self._compile(tactic, torch.bfloat16, a.device)
+        compiled(
+            _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E4M3FN, weight.data_ptr(), 16),
+            _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU, weight_scale.data_ptr(), 32),
+            _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E4M3FN, a.data_ptr(), 16),
+            _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU, a_scale.data_ptr(), 16),
+            _gmem_ptr(cutlass.BFloat16, out.data_ptr(), 16),
+            None,
+            None,
+            (Int32(n), Int32(m), Int32(k), Int32(1)),
+            current_cu_stream(),
+        )
+        out = out.view(*input_shape[:-1], n)
+        self.all_reduce.mark_published(out)
+        return out
+
+    def precompile(self, linear: torch.nn.Module, num_tokens: int) -> None:
+        """Compile the kernel ``num_tokens`` rows select, launching nothing."""
+        if not self.supports(linear, num_tokens):
+            return
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize
+
+        weight = linear.weight
+        n, k = weight.shape
+        device = weight.device
+        a, a_scale = flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize(
+            torch.zeros((num_tokens, k), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device),
+            is_sf_swizzled_layout=True,
+            alignment=32,
+        )
+        out = torch.empty((num_tokens, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        tactic = _selected_tactic(
+            a,
+            weight.t(),
+            a_scale.reshape(-1),
+            linear.weight_scale_inv_swizzled.reshape(-1),
+            out,
+        )
+        self._compile(tactic, torch.bfloat16, device)
+
+    def _compile(self, tactic: Tactic, out_dtype: torch.dtype, device: torch.device):
+        """The publishing kernel of ``tactic``, compiled once per device."""
+        assert out_dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        key = (tuple(tactic), device.index)
+        compiled = self._compiled.get(key)
+        if compiled is not None:
+            return compiled
+        cta_k, ab_stages, sfb_tmem_stages, split_k = tactic
+        all_reduce = self.all_reduce
+        multicast, stage_state = all_reduce.publish_target()
+        gemm = PublishingLowLatencyBlockscaledGemmKernel(
+            mailbox_multicast=multicast,
+            stage_state=stage_state,
+            tp=all_reduce.tp,
+            rank=all_reduce.rank,
+            capacity_m=all_reduce.capacity,
+            hidden=all_reduce.hidden_size,
+            acc_dtype=cutlass.Float32,
+            mma_tiler_mnk=(128, 8, cta_k),
+            num_ab_stage=ab_stages,
+            num_sfb_tmem_stage=sfb_tmem_stages,
+            sf_vec_size=32,
+            use_pdl=True,
+            split_k=split_k,
+        )
+        with torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index):
+            compiled = cute.compile(
+                gemm,
+                _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E4M3FN, 16, 16),
+                _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU, 32, 32),
+                _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E4M3FN, 16, 16),
+                _gmem_ptr(cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU, 16, 16),
+                _gmem_ptr(cutlass.BFloat16, 16, 16),
+                None,
+                None,
+                tuple(Int32(v) for v in (128, 8, cta_k, 1)),
+                make_fake_stream(),
+            )
+        self._compiled[key] = compiled
+        return compiled
+
+
+# FlashInfer's cutedsl_low_latency mm_mxfp8 takes at most 8 rows.
+_LOW_LATENCY_MAX_ROWS = 8
+
+
+def _is_low_latency_linear(linear: torch.nn.Module) -> bool:
+    """Whether the linear's 1-8 rows run ``cutedsl_low_latency`` (mxfp8_linear.install)."""
+    from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8LinearMethod
+
+    method = linear.quant_method
+    return (
+        isinstance(method, Fp8LinearMethod)
+        and method.mxfp8_cutedsl_override is not None
+        and linear.weight.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        and linear.weight.is_contiguous()
+    )
+
+
+def _selected_tactic(
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    a_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+) -> Tactic:
+    """The tactic FlashInfer's ``mm_mxfp8(backend="cutedsl_low_latency")``
+    runs for these operands: the autotuner's cached choice, else the runner's
+    default (the first valid tactic), as ``mm_mxfp8`` resolves it."""
+    # mm_mxfp8's private runner, tuning config and workspace (FlashInfer
+    # 0.7.0.post1), so the lookup hits the same autotuner cache entry.
+    from flashinfer.autotuner import AutoTuner
+    from flashinfer.gemm import gemm_base
+
+    major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(a.device)
+    runner = gemm_base._cutedsl_low_latency_blockscaled_gemm_runner(
+        major * 10 + minor, True
+    )
+    workspace = gemm_base._get_cache_buf(
+        "mm_mxfp8_workspace", gemm_base.DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE, a.device
+    )
+    inputs = [a, weight, a_scale, weight_scale, out.dtype, out, workspace]
+    _, tactic = AutoTuner.get().choose_one(
+        "mxfp8_gemm",
+        [runner],
+        gemm_base._MM_MXFP8_CUTE_DSL_TUNING_CONFIG,
+        inputs,
+    )
+    if tactic is None or tactic == -1:
+        tactics = runner.get_valid_tactics(inputs, None)
+        if not tactics:
+            raise ValueError("the low-latency GEMM cannot run these operands")
+        tactic = tactics[0]
+    return tuple(tactic)
+
+
+__all__ = ["PublishingLowLatencyBlockscaledGemmKernel", "PublishingMxfp8Linear"]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Low-M BF16 x BF16 -> FP32 GEMM in CuTe DSL: ``out[M, N] = x[M, K] @ w[N, K].T``.
+
+Two kernels: a one-CTA-per-column dot product (M and K compiled in) and a
+clustered split-K MMA kernel (shape-dynamic, compiled per (split_k, stages)).
+Kernels (_dotprod.py, _splitk.py) and the dispatch are taken unchanged from vLLM
+(vllm-project/vllm@75e3b17c, vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/cute_dsl/ll_bf16.py),
+with the tuned table of the DSV4.1 compressor projections.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import math
+from functools import lru_cache
+from typing import Any, Literal, NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_DEFAULT_DOTPROD_BS = 128
+_DEFAULT_DOTPROD_MAX_M = 4
+_DEFAULT_SPLITK_CONFIG = (6, 4)
+# Narrow outputs give split-K too few CTAs (one per 16 columns and split).
+_DOTPROD_MAX_N = 128
+
+# (K, N) -> {M: ("dotprod", bs) | ("splitk", (split_k, num_stages))}, GB300, cold weights,
+# CUDA graph, PDL; listed where it beat the default dispatch by >= 0.2 us.
+_TUNED: dict[tuple[int, int], dict[int, tuple[str, Any]]] = {
+    # DSV4.1 compressor ratio 2 (kv | score), N = 2 * head_dim.
+    (5120, 1024): {m: ("splitk", (4, 4)) for m in (5, 6, 7, 8)},
+    # DSV4.1 compressor ratio 1 (kv only).
+    (5120, 512): {5: ("dotprod", 128), 6: ("dotprod", 64), 8: ("splitk", (4, 6))},
+}
+
+
+class CompileKey(NamedTuple):
+    backend: Literal["dotprod", "splitk"]
+    M: int = 0
+    K: int = 0
+    bs: int = 0
+    split_k: int = 0
+    num_stages: int = 0
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def is_available() -> bool:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.hip is not None:
+        return False
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 9:
+        return False
+    try:
+        import cutlass  # noqa: F401
+        import cutlass.cute  # noqa: F401
+        from quack.compile_utils import make_fake_tensor  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def _use_pdl() -> bool:
+    from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import is_arch_support_pdl
+
+    return is_arch_support_pdl()
+
+
+def dispatch(*, M: int, K: int, N: int) -> CompileKey:
+    tuned = _TUNED.get((K, N), {}).get(M)
+    if tuned is not None:
+        backend, config = tuned
+        if backend == "dotprod":
+            return CompileKey(backend="dotprod", M=M, K=K, bs=config)
+        split_k, num_stages = config
+        return CompileKey(backend="splitk", split_k=split_k, num_stages=num_stages)
+    if M <= _DEFAULT_DOTPROD_MAX_M or K < 2048 or N < _DOTPROD_MAX_N:
+        return CompileKey(backend="dotprod", M=M, K=K, bs=_DEFAULT_DOTPROD_BS)
+    split_k, num_stages = _DEFAULT_SPLITK_CONFIG
+    return CompileKey(backend="splitk", split_k=split_k, num_stages=num_stages)
+
+
+def _fake_gemm_tensors(*, M, K, N, divisibility: int):
+    from cutlass import BFloat16, Float32
+    from quack.compile_utils import make_fake_tensor
+
+    x = make_fake_tensor(BFloat16, (M, K), divisibility=divisibility)
+    w = make_fake_tensor(BFloat16, (N, K), divisibility=divisibility)
+    out = make_fake_tensor(Float32, (M, N), divisibility=1)
+    return x, w, out
+
+
+def _stream():
+    from cuda.bindings.driver import CUstream
+
+    return CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+
+
+_compiled: dict[CompileKey, Any] = {}
+
+
+def compile_kernel(key: CompileKey) -> Any:
+    """Compile (once) the kernel for ``key``; must not run under CUDA graph capture."""
+    kernel = _compiled.get(key)
+    if kernel is not None:
+        return kernel
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+
+    if key.backend == "splitk":
+        from ._splitk import LLBf16SplitK
+
+        x, w, out = _fake_gemm_tensors(
+            M=cute.sym_int(), K=cute.sym_int(), N=cute.sym_int(), divisibility=8
+        )
+        gemm = LLBf16SplitK(
+            tile_n=16,
+            tile_k=256,
+            num_stages=key.num_stages,
+            num_dma_warps=4,
+            split_k=key.split_k,
+            use_pdl=_use_pdl(),
+        )
+        kernel = cute.compile(gemm, x, w, out, _stream(), options="--enable-tvm-ffi")
+    else:
+        from ._dotprod import LLBf16Dotprod
+
+        x, w, out = _fake_gemm_tensors(
+            M=key.M, K=key.K, N=cute.sym_int(), divisibility=math.gcd(8, key.K)
+        )
+        gemm = LLBf16Dotprod(k=key.K, bs=key.bs, use_pdl=_use_pdl())
+        kernel = cute.compile(
+            gemm,
+            x,
+            w,
+            out,
+            key.M,
+            key.K,
+            1,  # runtime N placeholder for the fake-tensor compile
+            _stream(),
+            options="--enable-tvm-ffi --ptxas-options -maxrregcount=64",
+        )
+    _compiled[key] = kernel
+    return kernel
+
+
+def ll_bf16_gemm(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """FP32 ``x @ weight.T`` for contiguous BF16 ``x`` [M, K] and ``weight`` [N, K], K % 8 == 0."""
+    # DLPack refuses tensors that require grad, such as an nn.Linear weight; detach is a view.
+    x, weight = x.detach(), weight.detach()
+    M, K = x.shape
+    N = weight.shape[0]
+    key = dispatch(M=M, K=K, N=N)
+    kernel = compile_kernel(key)
+    out = torch.empty(M, N, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    if key.backend == "splitk":
+        kernel(x, weight, out, _stream(), 1.0)
+    else:
+        kernel(x, weight, out, N, _stream())
+    return out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+from cuda.bindings.driver import CUstream
+from cutlass import const_expr
+
+
+class LLBf16Dotprod:
+    """BF16 router GEMM kernel based on CTA-local dot products.
+
+    This kernel computes C[M, N] = A[M, K] @ B[N, K]^T for bf16 inputs
+    and fp32 output. It launches one CTA per output column, distributes K
+    across CTA threads with vectorized loads, accumulates one fp32 dot product
+    per token, and reduces through warp shuffles plus shared memory.
+
+    :param k: Compile-time K dimension specialized into the generated kernel.
+    :type k: int
+    :param bs: Threads per CTA and K-stripe width used by the reduction.
+    :type bs: int
+    :param main_vec_width: bf16 elements loaded per thread in the main loop.
+    :type main_vec_width: int
+    :param tail_vec_width: bf16 elements loaded per thread in the vector tail.
+    :type tail_vec_width: int
+    :param use_pdl: Whether to launch with Programmatic Dependent Launch.
+    :type use_pdl: bool
+
+    :note: Supported A/B data types:
+        - BFloat16/BFloat16
+    :note: Supported accumulator data types:
+        - Float32
+    :note: Supported C data types:
+        - Float32
+    :note: Constraints:
+        - K must preserve 16-byte row alignment for contiguous bf16 inputs.
+
+    :note: K is handled as vectorized main/tail loops plus scalar remainder.
+
+    :compile-key: ``(M, K, bs)`` selects the token count, hidden size,
+        and CTA thread/K-stripe width specialization.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        k: int,
+        bs: int = 128,
+        main_vec_width: int = 8,
+        tail_vec_width: int = 4,
+        use_pdl: bool = False,
+        prefetch_pdl_weights: bool = False,
+    ):
+        """Initialize the dot-product kernel configuration.
+
+        This configuration fixes the CTA thread count, reduction warp count,
+        bf16 vector widths, and K-loop decomposition used by the generated
+        kernel.
+
+        :param k: Hidden size K used to specialize the K-loop decomposition.
+        :type k: int
+        :param bs: Threads per CTA and K-stripe width for the reduction.
+        :type bs: int
+        :param main_vec_width: BF16 elements loaded per thread in the main loop.
+        :type main_vec_width: int
+        :param tail_vec_width: BF16 elements loaded per thread in the vector tail.
+        :type tail_vec_width: int
+        :param use_pdl: Whether to launch with Programmatic Dependent Launch.
+        :type use_pdl: bool
+        """
+        self.bs = bs
+        self.main_vec_width = main_vec_width
+        self.tail_vec_width = tail_vec_width
+        self.use_pdl = use_pdl
+        self.prefetch_pdl_weights = prefetch_pdl_weights
+        self.num_warps = bs // cute.arch.WARP_SIZE
+        self._init_k_tiles(k)
+        self.main_prefetch_tiles = min(self.main_tiles, 8)
+
+    def _vectorized_elems(self, k_extent: int, vec_width: int) -> int:
+        vector_tile = vec_width * self.bs
+        return (k_extent // vector_tile) * vector_tile
+
+    def _init_k_tiles(self, k: int) -> None:
+        """Split K into vector loops, scalar rounds, and ragged tail."""
+        self.k_main_elems = self._vectorized_elems(k, self.main_vec_width)
+        self.k_after_main = k - self.k_main_elems
+        self.k_tail_elems = self._vectorized_elems(
+            self.k_after_main, self.tail_vec_width
+        )
+        self.k_done_all = self.k_main_elems + self.k_tail_elems
+        self.scalar_rem = k - self.k_done_all
+        self.ks_full = self.scalar_rem // self.bs
+        self.ks_part = self.scalar_rem % self.bs
+        self.k_scalar_full = self.ks_full * self.bs
+        self.k_part_offset = self.k_done_all + self.k_scalar_full
+        self.main_tiles = self.k_main_elems // (self.main_vec_width * self.bs)
+        self.tail_tiles = self.k_tail_elems // (self.tail_vec_width * self.bs)
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def _vector_dotprod(
+        self,
+        acc: cute.Tensor,
+        tA: cute.Tensor,
+        tB: cute.Tensor,
+        M: cutlass.Constexpr,
+        num_tiles: cutlass.Constexpr,
+        align_bytes: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    ):
+        for tile in cutlass.range_constexpr(num_tiles):
+            bt = tB[None, tile]
+            br = cute.make_rmem_tensor_like(bt)
+            cute.autovec_copy(bt, br)
+            br_f32 = br.load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+
+            for m in cutlass.range_constexpr(M):
+                at = tA[m, None, tile]
+                ar = cute.make_rmem_tensor_like(at)
+                cute.autovec_copy(at, ar)
+                vec_width: cutlass.Constexpr = cute.size(ar)
+                for v in cutlass.range_constexpr(vec_width):
+                    acc[m] = acc[m] + ar[v].to(cutlass.Float32) * br_f32[v]
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def _vector_dotprod_prefetched(
+        self,
+        acc: cute.Tensor,
+        tA: cute.Tensor,
+        tB: cute.Tensor,
+        rB: cute.Tensor,
+        M: cutlass.Constexpr,
+        num_tiles: cutlass.Constexpr,
+        prefetch_tiles: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    ):
+        for tile in cutlass.range_constexpr(num_tiles):
+            if const_expr(tile < prefetch_tiles):

+# Map a local smem address to the same peer CTA DSMEM offset.
+@dsl_user_op
+def set_block_rank(smem_ptr, peer_rank, *, loc=None, ip=None):

+# Plain DSMEM store; mbarrier helpers do not model this reduction.
+@dsl_user_op
+def st_shared_remote_f32(remote_addr, val, *, loc=None, ip=None):
+    i32 = _ir.IntegerType.get_signless(32)
+    addr_ir = remote_addr.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)
+    val_ir = val.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)

+        "r,f,=r",

+        ip=ip,
+    )
